messages.author: 37283d7785922c0c
messages.subject: Debugging shiny to JS Console
parts:
Hi all,
Not sure if it has been identified before, most of the posts I've seen on shiny debugging have been pointed towards dumping variables to stderr file outputs, and I hadn't seen any way to debug things to console, so here's an attempt that seems to work for most cases. The main idea is to use console.table() for dataframes passed as JSON, text variables passed as text for console.log() and a way to group them together using console.group().  I'm sure there's quite a bit that can be improved and cleaned from here but it provides a quick way to see variable outputs to the console!


ui.R:

library(shiny)
library(shinyjs)

shinyUI(fluidPage(
  useShinyjs(),
  source("DebugMe.R", local = TRUE),
  titlePanel("Old Faithful Geyser Data"),
  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(
      sliderInput("bins",
                  "Number of bins:",
                  min = 1,
                  max = 50,
                  value = 30)
    ),
    mainPanel(
      plotOutput("distPlot")
    )
  )
))

server.R

library(shiny)
library(shinyjs)
library(jsonlite)
shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  output$distPlot <- renderPlot({
    x    <- faithful[, 2]
    js$logme("DebugTab","group")
    js$logme(as.character(toJSON(head(iris))),"table")
    js$logme(input$bins)
    bins <- seq(min(x), max(x), length.out = input$bins + 1)
    hist(x, breaks = bins, col = 'darkgray', border = 'white')
  })
})


DebugMe.R

jsCode <- "shinyjs.logme = function(params) {
  var defaultParams = {
    obj : null,
    type : 'text'
  };
  params = shinyjs.getParams(params, defaultParams);
  
  if (params.type == 'table'){
    console.table(JSON.parse(params.obj))
  } else if (params.type =='text') {
    console.log(params.obj)
  } else {
    console.group(params.obj)
  }

}"
 
extendShinyjs(text = jsCode)

messages.subject: Re: Debugging shiny to JS Console
parts:
This is really nice!  I actually was going to provide a "table" argument in shinyjs::logjs(), which would use console.table if you want to display tabular data, but I decided against it because console.table() seems very broken to me (at least in Chrome).  (It only shows a few columns and can't scroll, it doesn't show the row names nicely, it's just not that great)

But this is very cool
